title: Getting started with `manifesto`
text: valid TOML manifest must contain following top-level sections: version: (required) match version manifesto package used generate . name: (required) name project. version: (required) version project. authors: (optional) array tables fields name, email, roles. r_version: (required) valid R version requirement string (e.g., “>= 4.2.0”). List core package dependencies (name = version). Optional groups: Named groups dev, suggests, ci, enhances, workshop, etc. contains set package references. package reference may : - version string (e.g., “>= 1.0.0”) - table source, repo, ref, url (e.g., GitHub, GitLab, custom sources) Examples:
code: gh = { source = "github", repo = "r-lib/gh", ref = "v1.4.0" } custompkg = { source = "url", url = "https://example.com/custompkg.tar.gz" }

title: Create Project Manifest Files
text: manifesto provides lightweight, portable way declare R project environments using simple rproject.toml file. makes setting sharing reproducible R projects faster reliable. lightweight, can also used easily setting new R installations workshops require packages. Unlike reproducibility-ish packages, focused able run code completely specified environment. aimed ensuring right sets packages installed users workshops.

title: Create Project Manifest Files
text: manifesto introduces human-readable, TOML-based manifest format R projects. captures: Project metadata (name, version, description, authors) Required R version Package dependencies, version constraints Package sources (CRAN, Bioconductor, GitHub, GitLab, Git, custom URLs) Optional dependency groups (development, workshop, full install) System dependencies (OS libraries) Install preferences (binary vs source installs) goal simplify project setup across local machines, teams, workshops, without locking users heavyweight tools.
